title: QuPath Digital Quantification of Liver Immune Cells
author: Xinle Wang
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bs6gnhbw
materials: Download open-source QuPath software from http://qupath.github.io . To avoid incompatible features in newer versions of the software, refrain from changing software versions during the same analysis. QuPath 2.3 Pete Bankhead

Open QuPath software and set initial preferences using the gear icon or from the menu ( Edit > Preference ). It is recommended to set "Set image type" as "Auto estimate" in Preference > General . This will enable the software to estimate image type as hematoxylin & eosin (H&E), horseradish peroxidase-based 3,3′-diaminobenzidine (H-DAB) or fluorescence without prompting user to manually enter for each image.

steps.title: Initialize QuPath Project
steps.instruction: Create a new project in an empty folder using the 'Create project' button. Import sample images by dragging and dropping them onto the QuPath interface.

substeps.instruction: Assign metadata to images using 'key' and 'value' (e.g., key = stain, value = CD68) for organization.
Sort images by right-clicking the project title and selecting 'Sort by... > key name'.

steps.title: Assess Stain Consistency
steps.instruction: Evaluate the sample cohort for stain consistency before quantification, as parameters must be applied to consistently stained samples.

substeps.instruction: Segregate samples into low and high sensitivity groups if non-specific staining occurs.

steps.title: Define Sample Regions of Interest
steps.instruction: Annotate the entire sample region of interest (ROI) using the magic wand icon.

substeps.instruction: Hold CTRL and SHIFT to avoid annotation overlap for artifact exclusion.

steps.title: Optimize Positive Cell Detection
steps.instruction: Optimize parameters for the positive cell detection module (Analyze > Cell detection > Positive cell detection) to capture individual cells and the positivity threshold for 'Cell: DAB OD mean'.

substeps.instruction: Annotate smaller sub-ROIs within the overarching sample ROI using the rectangle tool to save processing time (10-20 seconds vs 1 minute for whole image).
Capture varying ROIs depicting different degrees of background staining or different portions of the liver sinusoid.
If using QuPath v.0.2.3, set the 'Background radius' parameter to a negative value before optimizing other parameters.
Perform manual positive cell annotations using the 'Points' annotation function in a select ROI.

Use 'Measurement maps' (Measure > Show measurement maps), select 'Cell: DAB OD Mean', and use the scale bar to locate the optimal positivity threshold based on overlapping points annotation map color.
Validate optimized parameters by running the module on a second and third ROI.

steps.title: Save and Execute Detection Script
steps.instruction: Save the optimized positive cell detection script to the project folder for future access and batch processing.

substeps.instruction: Open the script editor (Automate > Show script editor).
Run the script (Run > Run) for a single image analysis.
For batch processing, select 'Run for project' and choose images (ensure images are closed in the viewer before starting).

steps.title: Exclude Artifacts
steps.instruction: Assess each image for stain and slide preparation artifacts and exclude them from digital analysis.

substeps.instruction: Option 1: Avoid artifacts during initial sample annotation by holding CTRL and SHIFT.
Option 2: Post-analysis, annotate the artifact, select all detections, insert detections into hierarchy, and delete the artifact annotation (without keeping object detections).

steps.title: Perform Locational Analysis
steps.instruction: Choose between concentrical or rectangular analysis to evaluate periportal versus pericentral immune cells.

substeps.instruction: For Concentrical Analysis: Locate and annotate liver lobule regions, set class to 'Other', and use the 'Save Annotation Script'. Run the 'Concentrical Partition Script' (input 'line length' and 'ROIName') to create rings. Use the 'Restore Annotation Script' if original lobule annotations need to be recovered.

For Rectangular Analysis: Locate portal tract and central vein regions and annotate using the rectangle tool. Use the 'Rectangle Partition Script' to divide the rectangle into 10 equal parts along its longest dimension.

steps.title: Export and Finalize Data
steps.instruction: Export detection results for all annotations (Export > Export Measurements) as .tsv or .csv files.

substeps.instruction: For liver lobule locational analysis, select 'Annotations' in 'Export Type'.
Select all detections, insert detections into hierarchy, and save to analyze positivity per partition.
